title: Reviewing a mock: error log, priorities and readiness

kcs.statement: After a mock, log every missed question with its domain and its cause (knowledge gap, misread qualifier or distractor trap), because each cause needs a different fix: relearn the topic, slow down on the stem, or practise the comparison.
Prioritise review by domain weight times miss rate: missing 30% of Domain 3 (34%) costs about 10% of the scored exam, while missing 30% of Domain 4 (12%) costs about 4%.
Treat yourself as ready when two timed, full-length mocks each score at least 80% with every domain at or above 70%, which leaves a safety margin above the 700 scaled passing mark.

problem_ideas: Mock 1 domain scores were 85%, 72%, 64% and 90%; compute each domain's weighted loss and pick the revision order.
Classify eight logged misses (given with your notes) as knowledge gap, misread qualifier or distractor trap and assign a fix to each.
Two mocks scored 82% and 78% overall; decide whether to book the exam and justify the answer against the readiness threshold.
Your overall score is 84% but Domain 2 is 66%; explain why you are not yet ready by this course's bar even though the exam itself is compensatory.
Most misses are misread qualifiers; design a one-week drill for that cause.
Estimate how many more Domain 3 questions you must get right to lift an overall score of 76% to 80% on 65 questions.
Turn three error-log entries into flashcards that test the comparison you got wrong, not the fact.
